baseHeader.methodology: Source-linked original summaries and reference-guided educational reconstructions. Models and motion are unvalidated; artist titles do not independently verify taxonomy. Navigation groups are not a universal kingdom system. Microbial behavior depends on strain and conditions. Expansion entries are individually referenced authored morphology studies; legacy Protista/Monera reporting categories do not replace modern domains. Actual screenshots, software checks and draft status are distinct from independent scientific validation.

before.summary: A large raptor associated with water. Fish, carrion and other animal food contribute to its diet.

anatomy.name: Adult head, bill and eye
anatomy.description: White head and neck, pale yellow iris and a hooked yellow bill. Detailed credited artist geometry is retained; eye surfaces are added. Proportions remain unmeasured.

anatomy.name: Feet and talons
anatomy.description: Yellow bare lower legs and feet with dark hooked talons. A separate standing posture supports both feet; grasping, prey capture and landing remain unavailable.

anatomy.name: Flight feathers and white tail
anatomy.description: Dark brown wing and body feathers contrast with an adult white tail. The detailed source atlas is retained; pale wing bands are corrected to adult dark brown. Fine vane relief is authored; individual feather mechanics are not solved.

behaviors.label: Fly
behaviors.description: An eight-second display study moves paired arm and hand wings, with mild hand twist and tucked legs, then returns to extended wings. Authored joint angles and timing are uncalibrated.

before.summary: A slender long-legged felid with a small head, solid dark spots and facial tear marks. The record uses the species-level binomial across its recognized subspecies; neither the artist individual nor the reference photograph establishes population-wide proportions.

anatomy.name: Small head and tear-mark region
anatomy.description: The retained surface has a compact head and dark facial lines. Exact skull, eye and nasal anatomy are unmeasured; teeth and respiratory physiology are not reconstructed.

anatomy.name: Slender trunk and spotted coat
anatomy.description: Solid spots and pale underparts distinguish the retained artist coat from rosetted cat models. Individual marking geometry, short fur and optical properties remain approximate.

anatomy.name: Digitigrade forepaw
anatomy.description: The paw and elevated wrist move on the same surface. Blunt semi-retractile claws require finer morphology; pressure, traction and claw retraction are not simulated.

behaviors.label: Walk · four-step study
behaviors.description: A bounded authored lateral sequence advances each foot with a separate support and recovery interval. The trunk progresses forward, and the sequence stops with all four feet supported. Corrected far-side stance targets prevent the previously detected distal-surface crossings at sampled phases; this is a limited geometry regression, not full collision validation.
behaviors.evidence: Source-linked qualitative study; authored positions and timing are unmeasured
behaviors.timeScale: uncalibrated authored display seconds; no physical speed or biological clock

rendering.reason: Qualitative four-step study; not a measured continuous gait. Joint ranges, contact forces, stride timing and tissue mechanics remain unvalidated.

behaviors.label: Rotary gallop | phase study
behaviors.description: Inspect one finite rotary sequence already in progress: right forepaw, left forepaw, a gathered aerial phase, left hindpaw, right hindpaw, then extended flight. The retained textured body bends through the trunk; limbs articulate at fixed-length joints, and supporting paws stay fixed relative to the ground. It pauses at the next forepaw contact. Four seconds is an authored viewing interval, not measured stride time. Foot clearance, lateral spacing, spine angles and travel are qualitative choices for this artist model; acceleration, stopping, hunting and force production are not simulated.
behaviors.evidence: Primary cheetah gait observations; authored uncalibrated articulated reconstruction
behaviors.timeScale: Four-second illustrative viewing interval, normalized model units
